## Overview

This model compares receptive grammar (`trog`) over one intervention-aligned window per child. The immediate arm uses t1 to t3; the wait-list arm uses t2 to t4. The model estimates the endpoint score given the onset score, age at onset and Block Design score. Each child contributes one row, so there is no child random intercept.

**The cohort contrast is an association.** The windows differ in age at onset, calendar timing and elapsed time. The immediate window averages 15.5 months and the wait-list window 14.2 months. Alignment does not equalise elapsed time or sessions received. Use the ITT suite for the randomised assignment contrast. Session dose enters only the separate sensitivity variant. See [the assessment-interval decision](../../../notes/202609212100-assessment-interval-lengths.md).

## Model

$$
T_{\text{post(aligned)}} \sim \operatorname{BetaBinomial}(n, \operatorname{expit}(\eta), \kappa),\quad
\eta = \alpha + \beta_{\text{cohort}}\,\text{immediate}
  + \gamma_{\text{own}}\operatorname{logit}_*(T_{\text{onset}})
  + \gamma_A A_{\text{onset,std}} + \gamma_{\text{ability}}z(\text{blocks}).
$$

One row per child (no random intercept). Priors follow the shared template in `priors.py`.
